steps.name: Invite TTL assertion compares at Postgres microsecond precision
criteria: RED: with the Background clock seeded at a value whose nanosecond part is not a multiple of 1000, the unmodified assertion fails with ttl_days = 6 on macOS
GREEN: a shared acceptance helper truncates an OffsetDateTime to microseconds; the step asserts expires_at - to_pg_micros(issued_at) == Duration::days(7) exactly
The whole member-invites feature and invite-accept feature stay green; no production code changes
steps.scenario_name: Submitting a valid email creates an invite and shows a shareable link
steps.description: Regression-first: seed the member-invites Background clock with sub-microsecond nanos so the 7-day assertion fails on every OS, then truncate issued_at to microseconds via a shared helper and assert the exact 7-day TTL.
steps.implementation_notes: See docs/feature/fix-invite-ttl-precision/rca.md. Precedent: 6b6bc0c (create_member_and_consume_store.rs:309-318). Do not switch the seed to now_anchor(); that hides the bug. Production stays unchanged.
